reason: Pi 1.5.2 reads before_agent_start prompt additions only from the systemPromptOptions object it passes in (runner.js emitBeforeAgentStart). Returning systemPrompt instead flattens the sectioned prompt and drops other extensions' sections.
Same host contract as above, for the prompt sections.
Unreadable or malformed credentials file returns undefined, which callers treat as 'no credentials'. A console.error would add stderr text to a normal path, and a throw would abort the job start.
Failed lstat returns false (not a symlink). Callers depend on that fallback; a throw or stderr line changes the result and output.
Failed lock acquisition returns false and the finally cleans up; callers depend on the boolean. Throwing or logging adds new behavior/output.
A failed git rev-parse (not a repository) returns undefined; callers fall back on it. A throw would break non-git directories, a log adds stderr.
A missing core.hooksPath makes git config fail by design; the catch swallows it so no custom hooks path is protected. A throw or log would break every checkout without that setting.
A failed git rev-parse --verify means the branch does not exist, which selects 'worktree add -b'. Throwing would stop creating new branches.
A failed rev-parse means base is not a local ref, and the catch falls through to the remote-branch lookup. Throwing would break remote-only bases.
The catch returns the job report with a 'could not be restarted' note as the tool/wake text; it must not throw because the report would be lost.
The watcher reports a step failure through ctx.ui.notify and keeps polling. Throwing would kill the watcher loop; console.error would corrupt the TUI.
A failing probe returns false, which callers use as the 'not alive' answer. Throw or stderr output changes that.
The catch removes the half-created job directory and rethrows the original error unchanged, so the tool error text Pi shows is exact. A console.error would add stderr output in the TUI.
The catch rethrows the original tmux error, or a precise 'needs tmux' Error for ENOENT; messages are tested/user-facing. Adding console.error would print new stderr text.
A launch failure is recorded into the job's output with exit code LAUNCH_FAILED_EXIT_CODE and the function returns false; throwing would skip settling the job, and console.error adds stderr.
A tmux probe failure falls back to the exit file or state 'lost'; job status values depend on this fallback.
An unreadable or invalid job.json returns undefined so job listing skips it; throwing would break listing every job.
Killing an already-gone tmux session is expected and ignored; a throw or log would fail every stop of a finished job.
A failed wrapper-liveness probe returns false (wrapper gone); the stop logic depends on that fallback.
A failed probe returns false, meaning 'not available'; callers branch on it, and logging adds stderr.
A worktree failure returns a { refused } result whose message is sent to the requester; it must not throw, and the message is existing output.
A missing or malformed granted.json returns [] (no grants); throwing would break requests without grants.
Killing an already-gone session is expected and ignored.
A failed probe returns false, which the broker uses as its answer; logging adds stderr in the root Pi.
A launch failure is settled into the job output with EXIT_LAUNCH_FAILED and serving continues; throwing would stop the broker, and logging adds stderr.
One failing request must not stop the others (documented); the catch swallows by design.
A failed 'command -v' probe returns false, selecting the next sandbox backend or the 'found none' Error. Throwing would break fallback.
An unreadable agent file returns undefined and is skipped; throwing would stop discovery of other agents.
A missing agents directory returns [] (no agents); throwing would fail when the directory does not exist.
A failed stat returns false (not a directory); callers branch on that.
A non-JSON output line returns { success: false } and is ignored while streaming; throwing would abort on any stray line.
A failed probe returns false, which callers use as the answer.
Killing an already-gone session is expected and ignored.
The output file may not exist yet while polling; the catch swallows by design (comment in source).
A tmux start failure is returned as spawnError in the result after cleanup; the caller reports it. Throwing changes the contract, logging adds stderr.
A failed probe returns false; sweep logic depends on it.
A failed read falls through to the repair attempt, or returns { unreadable: [] }; swallowing is the behavior.
A failed read after repair returns { unreadable: [path] } so the sweep quarantines it; throwing would abort the sweep.
The catch rethrows non-EXDEV errors unchanged and copies across devices for EXDEV; a console.error would add new stderr text in the sweep process.
A quarantine failure is appended to the job's output file with a specific message and returns false; throwing would abort the sweep, and the message is existing output.
A sweep failure is appended to the job's output file as a message; the process must still exit normally, and logging adds stderr.
An unreadable transcript returns undefined (no report); throwing would break job reports.
